structure.title: Our Strategy
structure.summary: This text outlines a strategic framework centered on portfolio transformation to unlock aspirations and achieve double-digit EPS growth. It details three strategic thrusts: focusing on organisational growth through portfolio segmentation into Core, Future Core, and Market Makers (with 80% of delta growth targeted from the latter two); excelling in five demand drivers (Social-first Demand Generation, Unmissable Brand Superiority, Multi-year Market Making, Channels of the Future, Winning in Many Indias 2.0); and accelerating future-proofing of distinctive capabilities, including disruptive science and technology, digitised distributive trade, net productivity, and a lean and agile supply chain. structure.title: Unilever Sustainability Agenda, Targets, and Circular Economy Initiatives
key_items: Stepping Up on Sustainability; Plastics; Nature
structure.summary: Unilever's global sustainability agenda focuses on climate, nature, plastics, and livelihoods, with India contributing to global commitments. Climate targets include net zero emissions by 2039, reducing operational GHG emissions by 100% by 2030, and scope 3 emissions reductions. Plastics goals aim to end plastic pollution through reduction, circulation, and collaboration, with targets for virgin plastic reduction, recyclability, recycled content, and collection. Nature targets include sustainable sourcing, regenerative agriculture, ecosystem protection, deforestation-free commodities, and water stewardship. Livelihoods goals involve smallholder farmers, living wage commitments, and SME growth. The page also features Project Circular Bharat, HUL's circular economy initiative, detailing its model, partnerships, toolkit launch, and achievements in waste segregation, social inclusion, and material recovery facilities.

nodes.title: Review of the Year
nodes.summary: The Home Care business achieved 5% Underlying Sales Growth with high-single digit volume growth in FY 2024-25, responding to softening commodity prices with price reductions and promotions, leading to negative pricing. Fabric Wash and Household Care both grew volumes high-single digit. Wheel's mass-tier brand used the Winning in Many Indias approach with differentiated marketing. Sunlight celebrated its color care promise with a Durga Puja installation. structure.title: Healthier India
structure.summary: HUL's Suvidha Model is a public-private partnership providing sanitation, hygiene, drinking water, and laundry services in underserved communities. It operates 20 centres in Mumbai, serving over 500,000 people, with women managing most. HUL and MoHUA signed an MoU to establish a Hygiene & Sanitation Centre of Excellence to scale learnings nationwide and strengthen climate-resilient sanitation. The initiative began in 2016 with HUL and BMC, expanded in 2020 with HSBC India to 17 centres, and now with JSW Foundation to 20 centres. HUL also runs behaviour change programmes. Impact includes 98% women feeling safe, ~50% reduction in diarrhoea, and over 180 million litres of water saved via solar-powered centres. It was showcased at COP28, acknowledged by WEF, and recognized by Harvard Kennedy School as a replicable solution for urban slums.
